text:
Jamie: Heads-up — customer onboarding hit a burst window and the sample app caused avoidable 429s. Sharing headers and the snippet that triggered it.
Alyssa: can you paste the headers?
Jamie: Sure.
Jamie: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 120
Retry-After-Ms: 120000
X-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-Reset-Ms: 1650000000000
```
Jamie: Sample app did `time.sleep(int(resp.headers.get('Retry-After', 0)))` so it treated the value as seconds. In some cases we also send ms variants and there's ambiguity.
Matt: yeah this has bitten folks before — `Retry-After` (seconds) vs `Retry-After-Ms` (ms) vs custom `X-Quota-Reset-Ms`. Our python sdk currently has a naive `int()` parse in two places.
Alyssa: Oof. And the sample app sync/async parity is inconsistent too?
Jamie: Right — sync sample uses `time.sleep`, async sample uses `await asyncio.sleep(int(...))` but both assume seconds. If header is ms we under/oversleep. Also no jitter or cap, so customers burst when they come back.
Sarah: TL;DR: three problems: header name variants, unit ambiguity, and missing helper utilities (sync+async) + docs on heuristics.
Matt: Proposal: add a single helper `parse_retry_after(headers) -> Optional[float]` that normalizes to seconds and understands `Retry-After`, `Retry-After-Ms`, `X-Quota-Reset-Ms`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Also add `sleep_backoff(seconds, jitter=True)` and `async_sleep_backoff(seconds, jitter=True)` to central utils. Keep typed signatures for mypy: `def parse_retry_after(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> Optional[float]:`
Alyssa: love that. Also add a `TokenBucketDebouncer` small utility in sample app for client-side smoothing — show sync+async usage. Many customers want a one-file drop-in.
Jamie: example snippet I want to add to sample app: ```python
# returns seconds (float) or None
wait = parse_retry_after(resp.headers)
if wait is None:
    wait = 0.1  # baseline
await async_sleep_backoff(wait, jitter=True)
```
Matt: tests: cover ms vs s vs missing header, negative values, and huge values (cap at 30s). Add doc recommending floor=0.05s, cap=30s, jitter=±20%.
Sarah: naming nit: prefer `parse_retry_after` over `retry_after_seconds` (more descriptive). For sleep helpers maybe `sleep_with_backoff` and `async_sleep_with_backoff`. Keep consistent with other sdk utils.
Alyssa: also need to update sample app onboarding guide to call out what headers to expect from Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (some infra emits only reset-ms style). That will reduce confusion.
Jamie: I'll update the sample app and the docs. I'll include mypy stubs and small typing tests for both sync & async helpers.
Matt: I'll open the SDK PR and mark it as a breaking-ish change in minor version if we expose new helpers. Add deprecation for any existing naive parsing functions.
deploy-bot: Created issue DEVEX-482 - "python sdk: robust retry-after parsing + sample app async throttle" (#1234)
Jamie: Thanks — assigning myself to update sample app, will link the PR here when ready. :thumbsup:
Alyssa: awesome, thanks. If you want I can craft the short doc blurb for onboarding (one paragraph + example).
Jamie: Please do. I'll paste the PR link here once it's up.
Matt: for implementation details: consider `int` overflow, non-numeric header values (e.g., '120s'), and timezone-agnostic reset-ms parsing. Also prefer returning float seconds to allow sub-second sleeps.
Sarah: good points. Keep the behavior deterministic for tests by allowing injection of jitter RNG.
Jamie: agreed. I'll include a small deterministic_jitter arg in helpers for tests.
Alyssa: :rocket:
